text:
A timid flock of storks,
gently folding their wings,
passed over the abandoned tower
in the light of dying twilight;

an hour when the Magician with his happy palette
pours beneath the radiant dome
pale shades of fleeting violet,
rippled by the wandering breeze.

Those birds unsettle me; in my soul
they rebuild my shattered joys;
they call up in my spirit the calm,
the solemn calm of better days.

The darkness of their eyes surpasses
even ebony's burning tones,
and their red-tinted beaks
join their alabaster throats.

The outline of their silken flanks
is a vague sign of mystical sadness,
calling to mind, when they stretch in sunlight,
the slow agonies of Whiteness.

With their garments of magical white,
with their languid, slender form,
their figures in the air resemble
the pale banner of Dream.

And if one, fleeing the claw that stalks it,
draws in its wing and stretches out its head,
it looks like a bow with a reddish arrow
that some hidden hand draws in the air.

In the glow of starlight,
in the sway of their weary flight,
they seem, beneath the concave vault,
blue bacchantes drunk on heaven...
